2020.08.09: Modified for use with GES6.
Laves-C15 becomes more stable than Laves-C14 again at high temperature,
as pointed out by F. Zhang et al. (Intermetallics, 9, 1079-83(2001)).
The claim by Zhang et al. that they need less parameters is nonsense, though.
This is probably a consequence of using a much too large temperature
dependence on the interaction parameters. This should be redone.
This is an example where the Kuba rule of thumb (H=3000*S) should not
be used. These are not simple excess parameters, but the energetics
of the defect structures (or lattice stabilities) mix in.
Laves-C15 even reenters as a stable phase above 4827 K.

The fcc interaction was set to give a solubility of about 0.03 at.% Ca in
fcc-Al at 600Â°C. The Al solubility in Ca (fcc and bcc) is then up to
The Gibbs energy expression for C15 from 05Ozt was kept. The corresponding
parameters for C14 and C36 use the same expression as for C15 keeping
the same difference in enthalpy as from the ab initio calculations and an
additional Delta-S inspired from the Cr-Zr system.
For C14: +1423-0.5*T J/mol-atoms and for C36: +453-0.3*T J/mol-atoms.
The above settings produced a narrow region of C36 on the Al-rich side of
C15. This was removed by adding another +100 J/mol-atoms to C36.

reduced to 1.2 at.% by adding an interaction. This is about twice as wide as
in 05Ozt. Corresponding interactions were also added to C14 and C36.

The parameters for AL8CR5_D810 used by 17Wan result in an incorrect site
occupancy with Al primarily on the second sublattice and Cr on the third.
Actually, the third sublattice should have mixed occupancy and the second
should be primarily occupied by Cr. When correcting this, the model was
also simplified to (Al)12(Cr)5(Al,Cr)9. The equilibria with AL8CR5_D82 are
retained, but AL8CR5_D810 is now much wider towards low temperature,
similar to e.g. 17Cui1.
The fcc interaction is modified to reproduce the same Cr-solubility
in fcc-Al as in 17Cui1, which is considerably higher than in 17Wan.
The fcc interaction is then much closer to the bcc interaction.
The maximum temperature for AlCr2 is reduced by about 40 K.
The dataset is modified from an assessment by L.Y. Chen et al., J. Alloys
Compd., 509, 1936-46(2011). However, parameters for Al-Cr are not included
in that paper. They, in turn, cite L.Y. Chen et al., J. Iron Steel Res.,
21, 10-16(2009), but this paper could not be found on the journal web-site.
This dataset is actually not too different from the 08Lia dataset.
The G(AL8CR5_D82,CR:CR) parameter is missing in the paper. There is some
difference in the equilibria between Al8Cr5_D82 and Al8Cr5_D810 compared to
the phase diagram published by L.Y. Chen et al. 2011.
Helander and Tolochko (J. Phase Equilib., 20, 57-60(1999)) showed
experimentally that there is a small region of B2 in the Al-Cr system.
Ordering with a TC of 1260 K and 1300 K was added by Subasic and
Dinsdale (COST), respectively. When adding this to the description by
Saunders, the bcc phase becomes ordered at low T as well and gets a
retrograde solvus and destabilisation of AlCr2 at low T. Dupin chose a
smaller ordering energy (without a stable B2 region) to avoid this.

notes: Dataset created 2023.07.11 by Bengt Hallstedt.
This is the 08Koz/95Aga dataset with a solution model for C14 and added
metastable C15, C36 and A12 from ab initio calculations.
Using the same interactions for fcc and bcc as for hcp results in a Mg
solubility in fcc/bcc-Ca up to 3.5 at.%, which is clearly too much. The
current value results in a maximum solubility of about 0.8 at.% and
minimal shifts of correspnding invariant equilibria; from 716 and 719 K
to 714 and 721 K.
The Gibbs energy expression for C14 from 08Koz was kept. The corresponding
parameters for C15 and C36 use the same expression as for C14 keeping
the same difference in enthalpy as from the ab initio calculations and an
additional Delta-S inspired from the Cr-Zr system.
For C15: +200+0.5*T J/mol-atoms and for C36: +127+0.2*T J/mol-atoms.
Without further changes, the C14 field is rather wide and there is a small
region of C36 on the Mg-rich side of C14.
Interaction parameters were introduced for C14 to have a total width of
about 1 at.%, and slightly asymmetric towards Ca. This results in
an additional C36 phase field on the Ca-rich side of C14.
The C36 field on the Mg-rich side was removed by adding a temperature
dependence to two Mg-rich compounds of C36. This is similar to what was
used by 06Zho, but with smaller numbers. The C36 field on the Ca-rich side
was removed by adding an interaction similar to that used for C14. Such an
interaction was also added for C15. These interactions are written using
wildcards. The use of wildcards does not result in any visible change, but
could be useful when extrapolating to a ternary.
The C36 tempareture dependence from 06Zho was reintroduced. Otherwise there
is a tendency for C36 to appear in the Al-Ca-Mg ternary.

Based on the assessment from P. Liang et al. 1998 with modified Gibbs
energies from S.H. Zhou et al. 2007. This was necessary because the heat
capacity of Cu2Mg (C15) from 98Lia2 increases too rapidly and makes Cu2Mg
stable again above 2800 K.
The Gibbs energy functions from 07Zho for C15_LAVES and CUMG2_CB are
discontinuous across the temperature interval limit. This was corrected by
adjusting the functions for the upper temperature interval. The other Laves
phase and CuMg2 parameters were reoptimised to reproduce the invariant
equilibria from 98Lia (and to some extent 07Zho).
The hcp interaction is very different from the fcc interaction. The fcc
interaction can be considered reasonably well determined since it is
based on a relatively well determined solubility of Mg in Cu. The current
hcp interaction gives a Cu solubility in Mg at the eutectic temperature
of 0.049 at.% Cu. The measured solubility is smaller (0.01 to 0.02 at.% Cu).
There are several measurements cited in Nayeb-Hashemi and Clark,
BAPD, 5(1), 36-43(1984), but they are all very old; 1931 or earlier.
Thus, the hcp interaction seems uncertain and the value from 98Lia seems a
reasonable compromise. The hcp interaction from 07Zho results in an even
lower solubility than measured and should not be used.
The parameters for the metastable C14 and C36 phases are modified to keep
the same Delta-G relative to C15.

Modified from 09Che. ZrB2 modified.
The elemental (ZR:ZR and B:B) stabilities of ZrB2 are missing. If they are
set to the standard +5 kJ/mol-atoms there is a huge ZrB2 phase field. If
they are set to zero (which makes no sense), the ZrB2 phase widens towards
B below 1000 K. I.e. 19Pan have used unknown large values. Since there is
no visible nonstoichiometry in their phase diagram the solution model is
removed here.
The experimentally observed structure for ZrB is NaCl type, but DFT
calculations in 09Tok show the FeB type to be considerably more stable
(-67 kJ/mol vs -40 kJ/mol).
